record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; notebooks and code were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README says it reproduces aspects of the original and reports results from refusal-direction extraction and ablation. The reported recursive ablation applies that approach to a new extraction stage.
record.gate_note: The README gives a 9-condition Gemma-7B-it ablation table. It also says refusal was induced by vector addition, but does not identify the model, prompt type, baseline, or numerical outcome, so that statement does not establish the V1 claim about inducing refusal to harmless requests. The notebook file names are not evidence that unreported experiments ran.
record.test_reason: Replication repo. It extracts a difference-in-means refusal direction in Gemma-7B-it, ablates it, and measures judged compliance on validation prompts, which is the original method. It extends this by extracting further directions recursively from residually refused prompts, which bears on V4.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also claim that the original paper's ablation and addition results are largely reproduced. They conclude that Gemma-7B-it refusal is mediated by a two-dimensional plane (r1, r2), with r3 and r4 inert, which favours a higher-dimensional account over a noisy-direction one.
record.recipe_differences: Replication repo. It reports direction extraction and ablation results, including recursive extraction on residual refusals, but the README does not specify enough procedural detail to verify an exact match to the original recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported recursive results are for Gemma-7B-it at layer 15, using 256 validation prompts and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct as the compliance judge; no alternative settings are reported.
record.problems: Evidence is README-only and code/notebooks were not read or run. The detailed table covers one model and 256 prompts; the stated sampling noise is ~3 points. The README does not report a general-capability check, and the addition result lacks model, prompt-type, and numerical details.
record.rows_left_out: No result rows omitted. The README's unquantified vector-addition statement was not entered as a V1 row because it does not state whether harmless prompts were used.

untested.parts: Inducing refusal on harmless prompts by adding the direction (stated only qualitatively). General capability preservation. Models other than Gemma-7B-it.
All; no weight edit or released abliterated model.
Affine, cone, or non-linear geometries; models other than Gemma-7B-it; layers other than 15.

missing.what: Claim that adding the vector induces refusal; model, prompt type and rate not reported
Direction norms (7.89, 4.70, 1.95, 1.21) and mutual cosines |cos|<=0.003 for r1-r4

record.verdict_notes: Evidence is README-only, one model, one layer. The README says every extraction used the same 256 validation prompts on which compliance was measured, so the directions are evaluated in-sample, which may inflate the effects. Two table rows have counts not summing to 256. Reported baselines: compliance is 37.9% with no ablation, which is far higher than the original's near-zero harmful compliance for Gemma, so the prompt set may differ. Dropped the reader's V4 limits_scope: inert r3/r4 bound the dimensionality but do not qualify V4.

versions.untested_parts: The table tests removal on validation prompts, but does not report general capability effects or numerical results for addition; the addition statement does not specify whether prompts were harmless.
No weight-edit or released-model abliteration result is reported.
No jailbreak suppression or training-against-ablation result is reported.
The reported evidence concerns recursive directions in Gemma-7B-it only; other geometries and models are not tested.
No separate harmfulness judgment is measured.
No language, model-variant, or base-to-instruct transfer is tested.
No refusal-training procedure or training stage is varied.

relation.reason: Its own ablation results bear on whether one direction removes refusal (V1) and whether a second direction adds removal (V4).

tranche.reason: Reproduces the original's direction extraction and ablation on Gemma-7B-it, one of the original 13 models. The measure is a judged compliance rate (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct) rather than substring plus Llama Guard 2, but it is the same construct. The recursive extension adds V4 evidence.

source_check.notes: The pack gives no [lN] ids for the verdicts, so label_id holds placeholders by version. Directions are extracted from the same 256 validation prompts that are scored. There is no random-direction control or capability check, and r1/r2 orthogonality follows from ablating before extraction. The vector-addition result appears only in words (no row). The README doesn't say whether ablation is at layer 15 only or at every layer. authors_conclusion is accurate.
